decisions.reason: As a recently launched carpet close to the existing assortment, it is cheap to keep as an option and there is not yet enough evidence to justify withdrawal.
This premium hand-knotted carpet fits the firm's design-led portfolio, and despite its niche positioning the uncertainty is still early enough that management would keep it on offer.
Although it overlaps with other new carpet introductions, it remains close to the core business and the firm can wait longer before deciding whether it truly lacks potential.
The corner bench is somewhat more specific in use and may be slower to prove itself, but it builds on established capabilities so the option is still worth maintaining.
This low-pile carpet faces some internal overlap risk, yet the cost of keeping it in the portfolio appears modest relative to the value of learning about demand.
The swivel shell chair line aligns well with the firm's move toward flexible workplace concepts, so management would likely continue it while market feedback develops.
